taxonomy.note: Current Kew POWO accepts Yucca pallida and describes it as native to east-central Texas.

target_zone_range.evidence_basis: Hays — Master Plant Pool Hays-local source flag. Burnet — USDA GRIN wild-material accession from Burnet County. NatureServe documents a north-central Texas endemic distribution but the additional listed counties found in this pass fall outside the current project target zone; NatureServe also flags the historical Travis report as doubtful.
target_zone_range.blocking_issue: Need one more exact native target-zone county.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Do not count planted landscape records or doubtful Travis occurrence as native county evidence.

morphology.look_here_first: Pale-leaf yucca forms low trunkless colonies of broad flexible blue-gray to sage-green leaves. The leaves are strongly glaucous, usually lack the curly white marginal fibers typical of Y. arkansana, and the flower stalk is a branched panicle rising above the rosette.
diagnostic_traits: pale blue-gray to sage-green strongly glaucous leaves
margins yellowish and minutely toothed or wavy
